**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 8, §8.1. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

A dataset is not a model, and model evaluation is not training. The central learning task selects parameters using past observations so that predictions work on new observations.

## Formal relationship

$$
\mathcal D=\{(\boldsymbol x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^{n},\qquad \hat y=f_{\boldsymbol\theta}(\boldsymbol x)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

For each shop order, x=(distance, item count) and y=fulfilment time. A linear candidate is fβ(x)=β0+β1 distance+β2 items. The six observed rows determine a dataset, not necessarily a representative sample of future demand.

## Interpretation and limitations

Generalisation is an out-of-sample property. A model can memorise training data yet predict poorly on a changed distribution, different delivery region or holiday workload.

## Explain it yourself

Identify the features, prediction target, model parameters and one possible source of dataset shift.
